identity.title: High-resolution observations of the symbiotic system R Aqr. Direct imaging of the gravitational effects of the secondary on the stellar wind

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present ALMA maps of radio continuum and molecular lines in R Aqr that show very clearly those effects at orbital and suborbital scales of $\sim$ 10-40 mas.

evidence.quote: Parallax measurements from SiO Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) data indicate a distance of 218 pc (cite: min14), although the distance from the GAIA parallax is 320 pc

question.value: How does the WD secondary gravitationally affect the AGB wind in the symbiotic system R Aqr, as seen in high-resolution continuum and CO maps?

findings_qualitative.value: 12CO shows two plumes along the E-W orbital direction resembling WRLOF spiral arms

evidence.quote: The shape and velocity of the plumes are similar to those expected for the projection in the plane of the sky of the spiral-like arms.

claims.hypothesis: High-resolution continuum detects both stars and mass transfer
claims.experiment: Long-baseline continuum map compared with predicted WD position
claims.result: Three components; C coincides with predicted WD position; B has a dust-like spectral index
claims.finding: Components A and C are the Mira and WD, and B is the first detection of mass transfer in a symbiotic system

evidence.quote: would be the first detection of mass transfer between the stars in a SS

claims.hypothesis: The CO wind is shaped by the secondary as in WRLOF models
claims.result: E-W plumes with velocity shifts of ~10 km/s
claims.finding: Strong equatorial confinement and a double spiral beyond the orbit

evidence.quote: We think that our CO maps directly show the very strong gravitational effects of the WD secondary on the circumstellar wind

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Hollis et al. WD position judged to be a jet blob, since it implies a semimajor axis 2.7 times larger than Schmid et al. imply

evidence.quote: The most likely explanation is that the claimed position for the WD in (cite: hollis97) is in fact an emission blow in the north jet.

limitations_admitted.value: Absolute astrometry ~3 mas; WD position uncertainty ~±7 mas

evidence.quote: we thus expect absolute errors $\sim$ 3 mas
